summary.text: Athenian democracy developed around the 6th century BC in the city-state of Athens, which included the city and the surrounding territory of Attica.
Participation was open only to free, adult male citizens, who probably made up no more than 30 percent of the adult population.
Reforms by Solon, Cleisthenes and Ephialtes shaped it, and Pericles was its longest-lasting democratic leader.

facts.label: Key reformers
facts.value: Solon in 594, Cleisthenes in 508-07, Ephialtes in 462 BC

facts.label: Longest-lasting leader
facts.value: Pericles, who led Athens from 461 to 429 BC

items.prompt: An Athenian reformer in 508 BC wants to break the unlimited power of the nobility. What does he do?

options.label: Sort citizens into ten groups by how rich they are
Ban every noble family from taking part in government
Group citizens into ten groups by where they live
Hand all power to one popular tyrant

items.explain: Cleisthenes broke up the nobility's power by organizing citizens into ten groups based on where they lived, not by wealth.

items.prompt: Two free adult residents of Athens live on the same street: a man who is a citizen and a woman. Which statement fits the Athenian system?

options.label: Only the man could take part in the political system
Both could take part, since both are free adults
Neither could, because only nobles took part
Only the woman could take part, since men served in the army

items.explain: Participation was open to free, adult male citizens, not to minors, metics, women or slaves.

items.prompt: Before Solon, government roles belonged mostly to aristocrats. On what new basis did his four classes work?

options.label: Every resident, slaves included, gained equal power
Noble families were banned from any role in government
Only the poorest class could hold any role
Property owned, not noble birth, now decided a person's role

items.explain: Solon broadened government to a wider range of property classes, giving formerly aristocratic roles to free citizens who owned property.

items.prompt: While his rivals were away helping the Spartans, a reformer won an Assembly vote cutting the power of the old council of ex-archons. What was left of the council's role?

options.label: It was abolished completely
It judged only cases of homicide and sacrilege
It became the main body writing new laws
It kept running the city's daily affairs

items.explain: Ephialtes persuaded the Assembly to reduce the Areopagus to a criminal court for homicide and sacrilege.

items.prompt: A friend says Athens was the first and only Greek democracy. What is the best correction?

options.label: Athens was first, but others copied it soon after
Athens became democratic only after the Peloponnesian War
Athens was democratic only briefly and never again
Other city-states had similar democratic constitutions, some before Athens

items.explain: Athens was not the only democratic city-state, nor the first; several others adopted similar constitutions earlier.

items.prompt: Many Greek cities had democracies. Why do most general accounts of democracy's rise focus on Athens?

options.label: Athens had the oldest democracy in Greece
Athens was the only city that practiced democracy
Athens left a fuller record, including a complete constitution
Athens had a democracy that included more of its adults

items.explain: Athens' system provides a fuller historical record, including the only complete surviving constitution, compiled by Aristotle and his students.
